subject: Admin activity visibility & delivery checklist — SIG questions
messages:
From: Lena Park <security@assuretech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Audit Team <audits@assuretech.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: admin activity extract for SIG/CAIQ responses

Hi Soojin,

AssureTech is working through the SIG and CAIQ requests for our Q3 procurement review. The security team needs an admin activity extract showing who performed admin actions (user created/role change/privileged action/role revocation), with the following details: timestamp (UTC), acting_principal (email), target_principal, action_type, resource_id, request_ip, request_user_agent, outcome (success/fail), and K/V cache identifiers where available.

Please confirm:
- What exact fields you can provide for a 90-day window (Sep 1–Sep 30).
- Retention metadata and how timestamps/zones are normalized.
- Export format (CSV/NDJSON) and integrity proofs (checksums/signature).
- Redaction options for PII (request_user_agent may contain device tokens).
- Typical delivery timeline (sample + full bundle).

We may need a signed chain-of-custody manifest for the delivered bundle. If you have a sample CSV and a short checklist we can include in the SIG evidence package that would speed review.

Thanks,
Lena Park
Security Program Manager
AssureTech
attachments: none
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Request: admin activity extract for SIG/CAIQ responses

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik and Marissa from Ops/Security for extraction details. High level answers upfront:

- Fields: we can provide all the fields you listed for the timeframe, plus session_id, request_id (internal trace id), and operator_role. We will include a mapping file describing any internal names.
- Timezone: timestamps are normalized to UTC in the export; we include original local tz in a separate column when available.
- Format & integrity: primary delivery is gzipped CSV with SHA256 checksums and a signed manifest (SHA256 + signature by internal key). We also can provide NDJSON on request.
- Redaction: we can hash request_user_agent or provide a scrubbed user_agent column; we can also pseudonymize emails in acting_principal on request but need a secure mapping table retained under NDA if you want reversible identities.
- Timeline: sample (one-day slice + manifest) within 48 hours; full 90-day bundle within 7 business days, assuming no additional legal hold requirements.

Attached: a preliminary field mapping (field_mapping_20270920.csv) and a recent 3-day snapshot sample (admin_activity_snapshot_20270915.csv) so you can validate format. Karthik — can you add the export hook notes (compression, checksums, TTL, and the script location)? Marissa — please confirm whether we need signed notarization for chain-of-custody based on past AssureTech engagements.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity extract for SIG/CAIQ responses

Thanks — a couple of technical clarifications from the extraction side:

- Export hook: we have a reproducible export job in repo infra/ops/exporters/admin_activity_export that produces gzipped CSVs partitioned by day. Script is: export_admin_activity.sh (we can include it in the bundle).
- Checksums: each CSV chunk includes a checksum file manifest_checksums_YYYYMMDD.txt with SHA256 hashes; the published manifest includes the signed hash bundle. We sign manifests with our key stored in KMS (signature included as signature.asc).
- Retention & TTL: primary logs are stored for 365 days. For the requested 90-day window we will pull directly from the daily blobs; we can also provide a 12-month retention statement for SIG.
- Columns (sample): timestamp_utc, timestamp_local, request_id, operator_principal, operator_role, target_principal, action_type, resource_type, resource_id, request_ip, request_user_agent_scrubbed, outcome, session_id, kv_cache_id
- PII/redaction: request_user_agent_scrubbed is the default; full raw user_agent is available in a protected bucket and requires extra approval. Acting_principal pseudonymization: we can produce hashed_principal columns using SHA256(salt + email). If AssureTech requires reversible mapping we will only provide under a mutual NDA addendum.

Attachments included in this thread: field_mapping_20270920.csv (maps our column names to SIG/CISQ standard) and a small sample snapshot. I will add export script and manifest to the final bundle.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer

Hi Lena — following up with the concrete next steps and checklist for the evidence package so you can add it to the SIG workbook: 

Deliverables (what you'll receive):
- Sample slice: 24-hour CSV (admin_activity_sample_20270915.csv) + manifest and SHA256 (within 48 hours).
- Full bundle: gzipped CSVs partitioned by day for Sep 1–30, 2027, manifest_checksums_20270920.txt, signature.asc, and a short README describing fields and redaction choices (within 7 business days).
- Chain-of-custody: signed manifest + checksum file (we can notarize via third-party on request; quote required).

Checklist for SIG evidence entry:
- Confirm the exact window (we have Sep 1–30 by default).
- Decide on pseudonymization vs reversible mapping for operator emails (default: hashed_principal).
- Confirm delivery method: SFTP (company endpoint), encrypted HTTP link, or shared GCS bucket. We recommend SFTP for immediate transfer; otherwise we will provide a presigned GCS link with 7-day expiry.

If this looks good I'll kick the export job after you confirm the window and the pseudonymization choice. I will also attach the export script and final manifest when the bundle is ready.

Thanks and happy to jump on a 20-minute call if you want to walk the SIG workbook together.

Regards,

--
Soojin Lee
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
